regions.name: Fernwake–Lantern road
regions.environment: Settled pasture gives way to woodland, marsh crossings and upland scree.

regions.name: The shifting flats
regions.environment: Seasonal channels, reed islands and exposed banks change where animals feed.

regions.name: The buried orchard
regions.environment: Abandoned fruit terraces, shaded pools and hollow old trees support a tangled food web.

regions.name: The dry shelves
regions.environment: Wind-cut ledges and short growing seasons favor reserves, grip and careful movement.

regions.name: The unmarked valley
regions.environment: Secluded forest basins, seasonal pools and cave streams reward observation.

verbs.intercept: Take an attack that was heading for another target.
verbs.interrupt: Stop or delay a pending action.
verbs.shed: Remove a bounded effect from an individual.
verbs.charge: A visible attack windup or momentum gain.
verbs.perch: Attach one small companion to one suitable host.
verbs.recover: Regain a bounded resource at a stated cost.
verbs.repeat: A repeated action or recorded pattern.
verbs.fall: A combatant becomes unable to act.

entries.name: Brindlehorn
entries.role: Herd grazer and established working companion.
entries.body: A low, heavy neck carries broad hollow antlers with blunt openings; its weight sits behind the head.
entries.habitat: Open scrub and grassland margins with enough wind to carry herd calls.
entries.diet: Coarse grass, tender brush and fallen orchard leaves.
entries.ecology: Antler chambers carry a low call beyond a rise. Herds keep loose contact without needing a clear view.
entries.behavior: Stops twice at a ridge: once to listen, once to set its feet.
entries.encounter: Existing depot companion and grassland wildlife; listen for the answering herd before approaching.

active.name: Antler brace
active.behavior: Shields itself and explicitly shields the wagon.
active.bound: Shield cannot restore lost HP or wagon integrity.

passive.name: Rooted
passive.behavior: Gains defense in a front position.
passive.bound: The extra defense does not follow it to the rear.

entries.counterplay: Disrupt its attack clock, attack the uncovered lane or force a formation choice.
entries.tradeoff: Reliable protection costs the party a faster attacker’s position.
entries.integration: Species, art and S28 kit exist. The expanded lore is a brief; S30 must integrate the kit with expedition costs.

entries.name: Reedskipper
entries.role: Social shallows dweller, swimmer and working companion.
entries.body: Broad body, webbed feet and a thick tail ending in a flat paddle; the tail changes its direction rather than acting as a sail.
entries.habitat: Shallow shelves, reed margins and side channels rather than deep open water.
entries.diet: Water shoots, soft stems and small shellfish found along the bottom.
entries.ecology: Feels a sideways current through its tail and changes course before its body is swept away.
entries.behavior: Pushes a floating object aside, then waits for it to drift back.
entries.encounter: Existing depot companion; Willowford observations and invitations already use its swimming ecology.

active.name: Paddle sweep
active.behavior: Interrupts a charging enemy and redirects its next basic strike toward Reedskipper.
active.trigger: Focus full; prefer a charging enemy.
active.bound: Redirects one basic strike, never an entire ability or a wagon-only attack.

passive.name: Give with it
passive.behavior: After redirecting a hit, advances its own next attack.
passive.bound: One response per redirection; no recursive counters.

entries.counterplay: Use steady low-pressure attacks instead of telegraphed rushes.
entries.tradeoff: Redirecting a strong hit puts its own HP at risk.
entries.integration: Existing species and legacy kit; this repeatable kit is proposed for S29. B5 later offers one learned channel or still-pool trick.

entries.name: Loamling
entries.role: Root-forager, food-cache maker and opportunistic scavenger.
entries.body: Compact burrower with broad digging forelimbs, a sensitive muzzle and soil-catching short fur.
entries.habitat: Soft margins below orchards and open woodland; shallow tunnels rather than deep cave systems.
entries.diet: Bulbs, buried roots and occasional spilled grain.
entries.ecology: Forgotten food chambers germinate. Its searching uncovers resources while sometimes undermining a path.
entries.behavior: Presses its nose to an ordinary-looking patch, then excavates a fan of soil.
entries.encounter: Existing companion and hungry road wildlife. Cache fans are the clue, not a glowing collection marker.

active.name: Underhook
active.behavior: Hooks under one opponent’s guard and briefly exposes that individual.
active.bound: Affects one enemy; creates no altered terrain or battlefield slot.

passive.name: Quick paws
passive.behavior: Its first attack against a newly exposed enemy advances the next attack clock.
passive.bound: Consume the opening once; it cannot refresh itself indefinitely.

entries.counterplay: Cleanse the opening or protect the threatened individual before the follow-up.
entries.tradeoff: Low staying power makes prolonged front-line fighting costly.
entries.integration: Existing species; S28 uses a Loamling as the raider, not this companion kit. S29 can test Underhook without B3 terrain mutation.

entries.name: Bellmoth
entries.role: Dusk pollinator and watchful companion.
entries.body: Broad folded wings make a hanging-bell silhouette; reflective scales flash briefly when a wing turns.
entries.habitat: Dry crevices beside pale flowers, mineral faces and woodland edges.
entries.diet: Nectar, mineral moisture and soft fruit juices.
entries.ecology: Dusk reflections guide it to flowers and sometimes to pale clay trail marks. Rain mats its wing surface.
entries.behavior: Opens one wing before turning, revealing a brief narrow flash.
entries.encounter: Existing companion and dusk sighting; observe where several moths circle rather than assuming every glint is a human marker.

active.name: Dusk shimmer
active.behavior: Interrupts the caller with a brief stun.
active.trigger: Focus full; prefer the opposing caller.
active.bound: The interruption wears off; it is not permanent control.

passive.name: Shimmer echo
passive.behavior: A successful stun gives Focus to the lowest-ready ally.
passive.trigger: An enemy survives the strike and is stunned.
passive.bound: One ally receives the gain; it does not trigger another passive recursively.

entries.counterplay: Field several independent threats so one interruption cannot halt the whole team.
entries.tradeoff: Fragile and weak at direct damage; its value depends on stopping a meaningful action.
entries.integration: Species, art and S28 companion kit exist. S29 should preserve its readable timing and S30 should price expedition effort.

entries.name: Cindercoil
entries.role: Shelter-seeking small animal with a stored-warmth defense.
entries.body: A rounded body coils tightly around a warm center; expression comes from opening and closing the coil.
entries.habitat: Insulated pockets under timber, stones and old depot walls.
entries.diet: Small invertebrates and fallen fruit; food and basking replenish stored warmth.
entries.ecology: Conserving heat matters through cold nights. Sudden displays spend a reserve rather than producing endless fire.
entries.behavior: Uncurls one small section to test a resting place, then folds back if it is cold.
entries.encounter: Existing soaked-nest recruitment. A warm empty resting dish can be a sign of past companionship.

active.name: Heat spill
active.behavior: Releases a concentrated single-target strike.
active.bound: A creature action, not a fire-type multiplier or a terrain effect.

passive.name: Warm follow-up
passive.behavior: Follows an ally’s interception with a short strike; its front stance also attacks faster.
passive.trigger: An ally intercepts; front stance changes basic timing.
passive.bound: At most one follow-up per tick; it cannot trigger itself.

entries.counterplay: Attack the open lane or interrupt Cindercoil when its defender is under pressure.
entries.tradeoff: The faster front stance exposes a frail body and can leave the wagon lane open.
entries.integration: Species, art and S28 kit exist. Biological reserve is flavor here, not an extra travel-food charge per hit.

entries.name: Slatewhorl
entries.role: Slow upland browser and territorial anchor.
entries.body: Overlapping living plates form a low spiral around a broad body; spreading feet brace the whole animal.
entries.habitat: Scree ledges with stable gravel beds and a few favored sunning places.
entries.diet: Low-growing lichens, hardy shoots and mineral-rich grit.
entries.ecology: A secure resting shelf is scarce. It blocks an approach to hold that refuge rather than pursuing intruders far.
entries.behavior: Turns through several deliberate shuffles; its plates settle with dry ticks.
entries.encounter: Existing track-and-assistance recruitment near the uplands. Circular resting scrapes identify a frequently used shelf.

active.name: Stone shelter
active.behavior: Shields one vulnerable companion, with itself as the fallback.
active.trigger: Focus full; prefer the lowest unshielded ally.
active.bound: Names creature targets only; it does not quietly repair or shield the wagon.

passive.name: Settled plates
passive.behavior: Absorbing a hit advances its next protective ability.
passive.bound: Bound the gain per attack, including multihit attacks.

entries.counterplay: Pressure an unprotected target or interrupt the slow protective cycle.
entries.tradeoff: Low damage and a slow attack clock make an all-defensive team vulnerable to stalls.
entries.integration: Existing species and legacy ability. This repeatable kit is proposed for S29, distinct from Moss’s explicit wagon shield.

entries.name: Hushgrub
entries.role: Small ambush predator; an alarming fighter rather than a worker.
entries.body: A blunt segmented body has broad pressure-sensitive belly pads and a narrow opening mouth; no eyes project above the soil.
entries.habitat: Wet root mats under reed beds, where vision is blocked but footsteps travel well.
entries.diet: Insect larvae, worms and tiny fish stranded in shallow mud.
entries.ecology: It locates repeated movement through the mat, then waits beneath the most regular source.
entries.behavior: A row of reeds trembles toward a footstep, then goes still.
entries.encounter: Look for movement against the wind at a recently exposed bank; watching safely records it.

active.name: Underbeat
active.behavior: Strikes the opponent that made the most basic attacks during the last short window.
active.bound: A visible target mark precedes the strike; it does not rewrite attack history.

passive.name: Still listening
passive.behavior: Gains a modest shield during a quiet spell without taking a hit.
passive.bound: A hit breaks the interval; shield cannot stack beyond the normal cap.

entries.counterplay: Interrupt the marked ambush or divide pressure among several attackers.
entries.tradeoff: Loses its advantage against slow, irregular attack patterns.
entries.integration: New design only. Requires a bounded recent-attack counter and visible mark, not a burrowed terrain state.

entries.name: Borrowbill
entries.role: Parasite-picker and potential symbiotic companion.
entries.body: A narrow hooked bill, short grasping legs and a flattened chest let it lie close against a larger animal’s back.
entries.habitat: Floodplain herds and the dry margins where grazers gather after rain.
entries.diet: Ticks, biting flies and loose skin removed from larger hosts.
entries.ecology: The host gains relief; Borrowbill gains food and a moving lookout. It cannot choose a perch that cannot carry it.
entries.behavior: Checks the same shoulder fold before settling beneath the host’s mane.
entries.encounter: A patient herd approach reveals it on a Tallowback. Gaining the host’s calm makes the small animal easier to meet.

active.name: Shared perch
active.behavior: Attaches to a willing large ally, giving up its own basic attacks for shared protection.
active.trigger: Focus full with a suitable unattached host.
active.bound: One host and one passenger; detaches when the host falls. No invulnerability or chained hosting.

passive.name: Clean coat
passive.behavior: While perched, periodically removes one minor disabling effect from its host.
passive.trigger: A bounded interval on the same living host.
passive.bound: Does not remove every effect at once or refill supplies.

entries.counterplay: Disrupt or isolate the host; pressure the passenger after separation.
entries.tradeoff: Two crew slots become one attacking body, a serious cost in a three-creature party.
entries.integration: New design and the bounded B4 symbiosis candidate, scheduled after S29. No dedicated art yet.

entries.name: Mireglass
entries.role: Wary wading hunter with a deceptive display.
entries.body: Long jointed legs support a narrow body; a thin side membrane turns edge-on, then reflects the sky toward the water.
entries.habitat: Bright shallow flats with intermittent open water and sparse reeds.
entries.diet: Small fish and swimming insects surprised beneath the reflection.
entries.ecology: Its reflection hides the shadow that would warn prey. The same turn can momentarily misdirect a land predator.
entries.behavior: Appears to vanish when it turns sideways, although its feet stay plainly visible.
entries.encounter: Still water with an extra piece of sky moving across it is the clue; a noisy approach drives it off.

active.name: False opening
active.behavior: Creates one decoy that takes the next incoming basic hit.
active.bound: Exactly one hit; area effects and later hits are unaffected.

passive.name: Glancing step
passive.behavior: After the decoy is struck, advances its own attack clock.
passive.bound: One response per decoy; decoys cannot trigger each other.

entries.counterplay: Use a cheap fast strike to consume the decoy before the heavy ability.
entries.tradeoff: Very little protection once the decoy is gone.
entries.integration: New design only. Implement as an individual decoy charge with clear UI, never an altered ground slot.

entries.name: Raftrook
entries.role: Brood-protecting wetland animal; some settlements keep it for eggs.
entries.body: A broad low chest rests on four paddle feet; two long folding side limbs hold gathered reeds close around its brood.
entries.habitat: Quiet reed islands that can break loose in a rising channel.
entries.diet: Water seeds, snails and soft reeds.
entries.ecology: It gathers and grips a small raft rather than building a permanent nest. Eggs survive short rises because the parent moves with them.
entries.behavior: Counts its brood with repeated touches before it will settle.
entries.encounter: Floating nests appear after high water; observe from the bank. Domestic eggs can enter later provision trades.

active.name: Draw close
active.behavior: Transfers part of its own shield to the least protected ally.
active.trigger: Focus full and a shield is available.
active.bound: Transfers existing shield; it never duplicates it or includes the wagon.

passive.name: Brood alarm
passive.behavior: Gains a bounded burst of Focus when an ally first falls.
passive.trigger: First allied fall in the fight.
passive.bound: Once per fight; no farming repeated revival events.

entries.counterplay: Strip its shield before the transfer or spread pressure so one transfer is insufficient.
entries.tradeoff: Giving protection away leaves its own slow body exposed.
entries.integration: New design only. Eggs are a food-web/trade direction, not an implemented laying resource or slaughter mechanic.

entries.name: Siltbelly
entries.role: Filter-feeding prey animal and a possible settlement food fish.
entries.body: A deep soft belly hangs below a small armored back; fine feeding combs fold into grooves beside the mouth.
entries.habitat: Muddy backwaters that stay wet when the main channel shifts.
entries.diet: Suspended algae and tiny organic particles sifted from the water.
entries.ecology: Its feeding clears small pockets of water used by other wildlife. The unarmored belly makes it vulnerable when lifted from cover.
entries.behavior: Closes every feeding comb at once when a shadow passes overhead.
entries.encounter: Clear ovals in otherwise cloudy water reveal resting groups. Best documented in place.

active.name: Close the comb
active.behavior: Folds its vulnerable feeding surfaces and shields itself.
active.bound: Pauses its basic attacks while folded; does not become immune.

passive.name: Silt purge
passive.behavior: Sheds one slowing effect when its folded defense ends.
passive.trigger: Its own shield breaks or expires.
passive.bound: One cleanse per cycle, not every damage tick.

entries.counterplay: Wait for the feeding surfaces to reopen or interrupt the folding action.
entries.tradeoff: A defensive wildlife kit with little offensive value and no planned travel utility.
entries.integration: New design only. B6 may introduce it as food through trade; observation-only does not promise recruitment.

entries.name: Stillmouth
entries.role: Large patient pool predator and dangerous combat specialist.
entries.body: A flattened jaw spans most of a squat body; sensory whiskers lie along the lip instead of projecting like teeth.
entries.habitat: Dark pools beneath exposed forest roots, with one narrow feeding approach.
entries.diet: Fish and young animals that return repeatedly to the same drinking place.
entries.ecology: Learns the rhythm of a repeated movement, then lunges into where the prey will be.
entries.behavior: Lets the first two disturbances pass without moving at all.
entries.encounter: Repeated missing ripples near a root overhang suggest a predator. Watching from safety can fill its record.

active.name: Third ripple
active.behavior: Strikes a visibly marked opponent after it repeats a basic-attack pattern.
active.trigger: Focus full; prefer a marked repeat attacker.
active.bound: The mark has a short expiry and only one stored strike.

passive.name: Remembered motion
passive.behavior: Reduces one repeated hit from the same source after observing that source.
passive.trigger: A bounded sequence of hits from one attacker.
passive.bound: The protection resets when a different attacker hits.

entries.counterplay: Alternate sources of pressure or interrupt its marked windup.
entries.tradeoff: Slow to establish a pattern, especially against varied teams.
entries.integration: New design only. Needs visible source tracking, not a hidden damage-type resistance.

entries.name: Gnawlock
entries.role: Climbing nut-eater with a stubborn close-contact defense.
entries.body: A short flexible body hangs from gripping forefeet; paired lower incisors can close around a tough stem without constant effort.
entries.habitat: Old orchard tangles where thin branches cannot support a heavy pursuer.
entries.diet: Hard nuts, seed cases and dry outer bark.
entries.ecology: Locks its bite around a support while the rest of the body shifts to another branch. Pursuers find it difficult to shake loose.
entries.behavior: Hangs from its jaws while calmly reaching for the next branch.
entries.encounter: Neatly split nutshells high above the trail reveal its feeding stations.

active.name: Latch
active.behavior: Binds one enemy’s basic attack clock while also slowing its own attacks.
active.bound: One target and a short duration; cannot chain a permanent bind.

passive.name: Lever bite
passive.behavior: Its next strike against that bound target ignores part of defense.
passive.trigger: Its own bind is still active.
passive.bound: Consume the advantage on one strike, including multihit cases.

entries.counterplay: Interrupt the grip or attack Gnawlock with a second creature.
entries.tradeoff: Trades its own attack rate for control and commits to one opponent.
entries.integration: New design only. B2 binding applies to a creature, not to the battlefield.

entries.name: Thimbleback
entries.role: Shy fungus-browser; an appealing small companion without a work requirement.
entries.body: A tall domed back encloses a very small face and tucked limbs; overlapping rim plates close like a drawstring.
entries.habitat: Damp fallen logs with sheltered dry cavities nearby.
entries.diet: Soft fungi, decaying fruit and tender shoots.
entries.ecology: Feeds in damp places but retreats to a dry pocket before spores and rain foul its breathing folds.
entries.behavior: Carries one uneaten mushroom cap around until it finds a quiet place.
entries.encounter: A tidy empty sleeping hollow beside a messy feeding patch reveals its routine.

active.name: Inward curl
active.behavior: Converts a bounded part of its shield into its own HP over a short recovery.
active.bound: No shield means no healing; attacks pause during recovery.

passive.name: Leave the coat
passive.behavior: Sheds one disabling effect when it uncurls.
passive.bound: One effect per cycle; no automatic group cleanse.

entries.counterplay: Break its shield or interrupt the recovery before it finishes.
entries.tradeoff: Excellent self-preservation can contribute little to saving an exposed wagon.
entries.integration: New design only. Its charm and behavior justify its existence even without a gathering or hauling bonus.

entries.name: Veilhen
entries.role: Flightless cover-nesting bird, prey animal and domestic food species.
entries.body: A rounded low body has a short neck and broad overlapping flank feathers that open outward rather than upward.
entries.habitat: Leaf litter below old orchard terraces and low brush at pasture edges.
entries.diet: Seeds, fallen fruit and small grubs.
entries.ecology: A sudden spread of flank feathers breaks its outline while chicks scatter beneath cover.
entries.behavior: Freezes with one flank half-open, leaving a gap for its young to escape.
entries.encounter: Scratched feeding circles and soft contact calls identify a family. Settled flocks supply eggs and meat through later trade.

active.name: Scatter display
active.behavior: Redirects one enemy’s next basic strike onto itself and gains a brief decoy charge.
active.bound: One attacker and one hit; does not hide the whole team.

passive.name: Make room
passive.behavior: An ally below half HP gains a little Focus when Veilhen takes the redirected hit.
passive.bound: One lowest-health ally; no recursive reaction.

entries.counterplay: Follow the small redirected strike with another source of pressure.
entries.tradeoff: Protective misdirection is fragile when several attackers act together.
entries.integration: New design only. Food use belongs to B6 trade/encounter work, not automatic meat after every battle.

entries.name: Sapstilt
entries.role: Patient orchard ambush insect and specialist fighter.
entries.body: A narrow body stands on long angular legs; flattened joints align with broken twigs when it settles.
entries.habitat: Old sap wounds and fruit splits where feeding insects return repeatedly.
entries.diet: Sap-feeding insects; sugary moisture supplements scarce prey.
entries.ecology: Waits at a reliable feeding place instead of chasing. The first precise movement matters more than sustained speed.
entries.behavior: Moves one foot at a time while the rest of the body stays perfectly aligned.
entries.encounter: An apparent twig changes which fruit split it points toward between observations.

active.name: Patient strike
active.behavior: A long windup delivers a strong single hit if uninterrupted.
active.bound: Taking a direct hit during the windup reduces its payoff.

passive.name: Still outline
passive.behavior: The first basic attack directed at it is delayed briefly.
passive.trigger: First time an enemy selects it.
passive.bound: Once per fight; named attacks that explicitly reveal it ignore the delay.

entries.counterplay: Apply an early inexpensive hit, then keep interrupting the windup.
entries.tradeoff: Little defense after its first concealment and poor response to scattered targets.
entries.integration: New design only. A visible per-creature windup and spent concealment indicator are required.

entries.name: Guttersail
entries.role: Ravine glider, quick hunter and potential speed specialist.
entries.body: A deep membrane folds down the sides of a slender body; long forelimbs open it like a gutter catching rising air.
entries.habitat: Narrow ravines with brief updrafts and many grounded resting ledges.
entries.diet: Flying insects and small shelf-dwelling animals.
entries.ecology: Most travel happens in short lifts between ledges. A spectacular dive must be followed by an awkward grounded recovery.
entries.behavior: Tests a draft with one membrane edge before opening both sides.
entries.encounter: A scrape high on one ledge and another much lower across the gap reveal a landing route.

active.name: Folded dive
active.behavior: Spends accumulated momentum on a strong strike, then becomes exposed briefly.
active.bound: Momentum has a cap; the recovery cannot be skipped by immediately recasting.

passive.name: Find the lift
passive.behavior: Uninterrupted attacks build a small momentum reserve.
passive.bound: Interruptions remove part of the reserve; no terrain bonus is required.

entries.counterplay: Interrupt it before the dive or concentrate pressure during grounded recovery.
entries.tradeoff: Speed creates a predictable vulnerable window.
entries.integration: New design only. Momentum is an individual resource, not a new creature type or field-weather state.

entries.name: Tallowback
entries.role: Drought-country herd grazer; domestic milk and meat animal in some settlements.
entries.body: Short sturdy legs carry a heavy back with visible reserve folds; its head stays low while it walks.
entries.habitat: Dry pasture and shelves, descending to floodplain margins after scarce rain.
entries.diet: Tough dry grasses and seed heads; long grazing supports stored reserves.
entries.ecology: Survives lean seasons by spending body reserves slowly. A defending parent can expend them much faster.
entries.behavior: Refuses a fresh patch until the herd has finished the one underfoot.
entries.encounter: Broad grazing lines converge at a reliable water approach. Domestic animals can appear at provision markets.

active.name: Spend the reserve
active.behavior: Converts part of an internal reserve into self-protection.
active.bound: Reserve is finite within a fight; no repeated consumption of expedition food.

passive.name: Keep grazing
passive.behavior: Builds a small reserve during intervals without taking damage.
passive.bound: Reserve cannot exceed its cap or carry an infinite battle stall.

entries.counterplay: Keep steady pressure on it so reserve cannot recover.
entries.tradeoff: A tough body with little burst damage; reserve exhaustion is visible.
entries.integration: New design only. B6 supports settlement food trade; B4 may use its body as a Borrowbill host.

entries.name: Rattleloom
entries.role: Solitary gully hunter and binding specialist.
entries.body: A low many-jointed body has broad grasping ends on two limbs and fine fiber-producing grooves beneath the abdomen.
entries.habitat: Loose-stone gullies where moving pebbles announce passing prey.
entries.diet: Small crawling invertebrates caught near its listening fibers.
entries.ecology: Suspended pebbles transmit movement through taut fibers. It holds its own listening rig rather than changing the entire ground.
entries.behavior: Lifts one pebble to silence it while listening through another.
entries.encounter: A pebble hangs just clear of the ground without wind moving it.

active.name: Catch the rush
active.behavior: Binds one charging opponent and exposes it to a follow-up.
active.trigger: Focus full; prefer a charging target.
active.bound: Short individual bind only; no battlefield trap, changed tile or permanent terrain state.

passive.name: Taut line
passive.behavior: Gains a small shield when an ally strikes its currently bound target.
passive.trigger: An allied basic hit on that target.
passive.bound: One gain per binding cycle, not a response to its own strike.

entries.counterplay: Use a low-commitment attack to interrupt the catch or cleanse the bind.
entries.tradeoff: A poor direct attacker if the team cannot use the brief opening.
entries.integration: New design only. This is the B2 combination candidate; explicitly respects the rejection of B3.

entries.name: Chalkmaw
entries.role: Territorial cliff browser with an unusually forceful bite.
entries.body: A broad chisel jaw sits close to the ground; powerful cheek muscles make the head wider than the shoulders.
entries.habitat: Sparse ledges with hard lichen crusts and wind-polished surfaces.
entries.diet: Lichens and tough shelf plants scraped with the jaw edge.
entries.ecology: Grinding through hard food favors force over speed. The jaw needs a pause after a full bite.
entries.behavior: Wipes the lower jaw against a ledge, leaving paired pale streaks.
entries.encounter: Follow scrape marks, then watch whether they face a feeding patch or an approach it is guarding.

active.name: Shear bite
active.behavior: Ignores a portion of one target’s defense on a heavy strike.
active.bound: The follow-up recovery slows its basic attacks; no universal armor immunity.

passive.name: Reset the jaw
passive.behavior: After an uninterrupted recovery, its next basic hit gains a modest bonus.
passive.bound: One stored hit, lost if interrupted before use.

entries.counterplay: Interrupt recovery or protect against a single large strike instead of relying only on defense.
entries.tradeoff: Strong against armor, unreliable against frequent disruption.
entries.integration: New design only. Its geology explains its feeding anatomy, not a stone-element classification.

entries.name: Foldwake
entries.role: Secretive pool-edge predator with an explosive first movement.
entries.body: Six long limbs fold flat along a broad ribbon-like body; opened, the animal is much taller than its resting outline.
entries.habitat: Seasonal forest pools with narrow damp hollows beneath fallen timber.
entries.diet: Small pool animals and invertebrates sheltering under wet logs.
entries.ecology: The flattened resting shape fits disappearing pools and hides its true reach from passing prey.
entries.behavior: A thin dark seam under a log briefly becomes a tall shape, then folds away.
entries.encounter: Observe a shallow pool as it drains; do not assume every hollow is empty.

active.name: Unfurl
active.behavior: A clearly telegraphed long-reach strike can reach a rear opponent.
active.bound: Long windup; an interruption cancels the reach advantage.

passive.name: Fold away
passive.behavior: Gains brief protection after completing a strike.
passive.bound: Protection ends before its next windup; no permanent hiding.

entries.counterplay: Interrupt the windup or prepare protection for the announced rear target.
entries.tradeoff: Predictable cycle and weak sustained basic attacks.
entries.integration: New design only. An observation-first threat; recruitment is not promised.

entries.name: Mourningrail
entries.role: Forest call-mimic and possible unpredictable companion.
entries.body: A long throat folds against a slim chest; a short fan of tail feathers opens when it listens rather than when it calls.
entries.habitat: Layered forest margins where distant calls are clearer than silhouettes.
entries.diet: Berries, insects and fallen seeds.
entries.ecology: Imitates useful contact and alarm calls to move between feeding groups. A poor imitation attracts unwanted attention.
entries.behavior: Repeats only the last part of a call, leaving a recognizable gap.
entries.encounter: A familiar creature’s call comes from the wrong height or answers itself too quickly.

active.name: Borrowed phrase
active.behavior: Echoes a reduced version of the last eligible ally ability.
active.trigger: Focus full with a recorded eligible ability.
active.bound: Cannot copy copies, consumables, revival or attachment; the eligible set is explicit.

passive.name: Listen first
passive.behavior: Gains a little Focus when a different ally casts.
passive.bound: Once per source in a short window; echo casts do not feed the loop.

entries.counterplay: Interrupt it after a useful ally cast or exploit the weak fallback when no ability can be copied.
entries.tradeoff: Its value depends on team order; copying must not become a universally best fourth ability.
entries.integration: New design only. Higher implementation risk: bounded eligible effect copying needs dedicated tests before runtime content.

entries.name: Trenchwink
entries.role: Small drought sleeper and resilient prey animal.
entries.body: A narrow soft body tucks short limbs into sealed folds; translucent eyelid caps close over a small face.
entries.habitat: Seasonal drainage trenches where damp pockets outlast surface water.
entries.diet: Tiny crustaceans and soft shoots exposed as water retreats.
entries.ecology: Brief dormancy lets it endure drying pools. It must choose when to reopen, because recovery leaves it vulnerable.
entries.behavior: Seems inert until a faint blink passes beneath a sealed eyelid cap.
entries.encounter: After rain, seemingly empty drainage cracks begin producing fresh feeding trails.

active.name: Open again
active.behavior: Recovers a little HP while becoming briefly exposed.
active.bound: The recovery never repairs the wagon or revives an ally.

passive.name: Last damp pocket
passive.behavior: The first lethal hit leaves it dormant at minimal HP for a short interval.
passive.bound: Once per fight; no attacks or protection of the wagon while dormant, and defeat detection must remain bounded.

entries.counterplay: Wait out dormancy and pressure the exposed recovery instead of wasting a large hit.
entries.tradeoff: Staying alive does not guarantee useful damage or wagon defense.
entries.integration: New design only. Dormancy must be visible and must not create a soft-lock or repeatable resurrection loop.

entries.name: Knellfin
entries.role: Cave-stream hunter adapted to darkness.
entries.body: A narrow fish has an enlarged throat chamber and low fins held close to its body; its jaw opens sideways into a broad listening surface.
entries.habitat: Dark cave channels and sheltered pools at the edge of the unmarked valley.
entries.diet: Small fish and drifting cave invertebrates.
entries.ecology: A throat pulse returns from nearby bodies. Closely spaced echoes reveal moving prey without sight.
entries.behavior: A small surface ring appears, followed by another from beneath an overhang.
entries.encounter: Record the repeated rings at a cave entrance. Its aquatic life does not justify a mandatory tank on every wagon.

active.name: Aftertone
active.behavior: A strike leaves one delayed second pulse on its announced target.
active.bound: One delayed pulse per cast; the pulse cannot schedule another pulse.

passive.name: Read the echo
passive.behavior: The pulse is stronger against an exposed target.
passive.bound: No bonus on the initial strike; keep source attribution after a knockout.

entries.counterplay: Shield the marked target before the delayed pulse or clear the exposure.
entries.tradeoff: Damage arrives late and may be wasted if the target is already out.
entries.integration: New design only. Requires one bounded delayed action record; no elemental sonic class.
